sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ramesh Kumar Chaurasia
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 321 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506, 406 IPC, Police Station Rasara, District Ballia with the prayer to enlarge her on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
According to prosecution version applicant and co-accused persons have taken an amount of Rs.3,60,000/- from the complainant on the pretext of providing a job in Income Tax Department.
Learned counsel submitted that only an amount of Rs.80,000/- has been transferred in the account of applicant.
The allegations leveled against the applicant are wholly false.

sentences.text: The First Information Report of this case was got lodged by moving an application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
It was further submitted that applicant is an unmarried young lady.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 24.03.2025.
The applicant has no criminal history.
It was submitted that in case applicant is granted bail, she shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would co-operate during trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that in view of allegations made against applicant, she is not entitled for bail.
5. I have considered rival submissions and perused the record.
6. It is well settled that at pre-conviction stage, there is presumption of innocence.
The object of keeping a person in custody is to ensure his availability to face the trial and to receive the sentence that may be passed.
The detention is not supposed to be punitive or preventive.
Seriousness of the allegation or the availability of material in support thereof are not the only considerations for declining bail.

In this connection reference may be made to case of Vinod Bhandari V State of M.P.
(2015) 11 Supreme Court Cases 502.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In the instant matter, considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
According bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Kumari Chandani Chauhan, involved in aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
(i). The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant shall not pressurize / intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii).
The applicant shall appear before the Trial Court on the date fixed, unless her personal appearance is exempted.

(iv). The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court.
9. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
